*All Out (2021)* was the **third annual** event in All Elite Wrestling's (AEW) **All Out** pay-per-view (PPV) chronology. It took place on **September 5, 2021**, at the **Now Arena** in Hoffman Estates, Illinois (a suburb of Chicago). The event was a major success for AEW, featuring high-profile matches, shocking moments, and significant storyline developments.

---

### **Key Details**
- **Date:** September 5, 2021
- **Venue:** Now Arena (Hoffman Estates, Illinois)
- **Attendance:** ~10,000 (sold out)
- **Buyrate:** One of AEW's highest-grossing PPVs at the time (exact numbers not officially disclosed).
- **Main Event:** **Kenny Omega (c) vs. Christian Cage** for the **AEW World Championship**.
- **Other Major Matches:**
  - **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** (Punk’s first AEW match)
  - **Chris Jericho vs. MJF** (Jericho’s "Labors of Jericho" challenge)
  - **Bryan Danielson vs. Kenny Omega** (for the **AEW World Championship #1 Contender’s spot**)
  - **The Young Bucks (Matt & Nick Jackson) (c) vs. Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix)** for the **AEW World Tag Team Championships** (Steel Cage Match)
  - **Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. (c) vs. Kris Statlander** for the **AEW Women’s World Championship**

---

### **Full Match Card & Results**
*(Winners in **bold**)*

1. **Pre-Show (Buy-In) Matches:**
   - **Jurassic Express (Jungle Boy & Luchasaurus) & Marko Stunt vs. The Hardy Family Office (Private Party & The Blade)** – **Jurassic Express won** (6-man tag)
   - **Miro (c) vs. Fuego Del Sol** – **Miro retained** the **AEW TNT Championship** (squash)
   - **Paul Wight vs. QT Marshall (w/ Aaron Solow & Nick Comoroto)** – **Wight won** (squash)

2. **Main Card Matches:**
   - **The Young Bucks (c) vs. Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo & Rey Fénix)** – **Lucha Brothers won** to become **AEW World Tag Team Champions** (Steel Cage Match)
   - **Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. (c) vs. Kris Statlander** – **Baker retained** the **AEW Women’s World Championship**
   - **Jon Moxley vs. Satoshi Kojima** – **Moxley won** (singles match)
   - **CM Punk vs. Darby Allin** – **Punk won** (singles match)
   - **Chris Jericho vs. MJF** – **MJF won** (singles match, Jericho’s "Labors of Jericho" challenge)
   - **Bryan Danielson vs. Kenny Omega** – **No Contest** (time-limit draw, Danielson earned a future title shot)
   - **Kenny Omega (c) vs. Christian Cage** – **Omega retained** the **AEW World Championship**

---

### **Major Storylines & Highlights**

#### **1. CM Punk’s AEW Debut & Match vs. Darby Allin**
- **CM Punk** made his **long-awaited AEW debut** on the **August 20, 2021, episode of *Dynamite*** (after a 7-year WWE hiatus), cutting a scathing promo on WWE and challenging Darby Allin to a match at **All Out**.
- The match was **highly anticipated** and delivered, with Punk winning in **~15 minutes** after hitting the **GTS (Go To Sleep)**.
- Punk’s return was a **huge ratings boost** for AEW, drawing **1.1 million viewers** for his debut promo.
- Post-match, Punk was **attacked by The Elite (Kenny Omega, The Young Bucks, and Adam Cole)**, leading to a **temporary alliance with Darby Allin and Sting**.

#### **2. The Young Bucks vs. Lucha Brothers (Steel Cage Match)**
- The **Lucha Brothers (Penta & Fénix)** won the **AEW World Tag Team Championships** in a **brutal Steel Cage Match**, ending the Young Bucks’ **302-day reign**.
- The match featured **high-risk spots**, including a **Fénix moonsault from the top of the cage** onto the Bucks.
- This was a **huge moment** for the Lucha Brothers, who had been chasing the titles for months.

#### **3. Bryan Danielson’s AEW Debut & Match vs. Kenny Omega**
- **Bryan Danielson (formerly Daniel Bryan in WWE)** made his **shocking AEW debut** on the **September 3, 2021, episode of *Rampage***, immediately challenging Kenny Omega to a match at **All Out**.
- The match was a **technical masterpiece**, ending in a **30-minute time-limit draw** (the first in AEW history).
- Post-match, **Tony Khan announced that Danielson would get a future AEW World Championship match** (which he later won at **Winter Is Coming 2021**).

#### **4. Chris Jericho vs. MJF (Labors of Jericho)**
- **MJF** had been **tormenting Jericho** for months, forcing him to complete **"Labors"** (similar to the 12 Labors of Hercules) to earn a match.
- Jericho **completed all challenges** (including a **10-man tag match** and a **battle royal**), but **MJF cheated to win** at All Out by **hitting Jericho with his own bat (Judas Effect)**.
- This led to **MJF joining The Inner Circle** (before later betraying them).

#### **5. Kenny Omega vs. Christian Cage (AEW World Championship)**
- **Christian Cage** had been on a **hot streak**, winning the **AEW TNT Championship** and then challenging Omega for the **AEW World Title**.
- Omega **retained** after **Don Callis interfered**, setting up future **Omega vs. Danielson** and **Omega vs. Hangman Page** matches.

#### **6. Britt Baker vs. Kris Statlander (AEW Women’s Title)**
- **Britt Baker** retained her title in a **hard-hitting match**, further establishing herself as AEW’s **top women’s star**.
- This was part of Baker’s **dominant 2021 run**, which included **feuds with Thunder Rosa and Ruby Soho**.

---

### **Post-Event Fallout & Impact**
- **CM Punk’s feud with The Elite** continued, leading to **Punk vs. Omega at Full Gear 2021** (though it was later scrapped due to Punk’s injury).
- **Bryan Danielson’s title shot** was set for **Winter Is Coming 2021**, where he **defeated Omega** in a **60-minute Iron Man Match** (though Omega retained due to a time-limit draw, then lost the title to **Adam Page**).
- **MJF’s betrayal of The Inner Circle** led to the **formation of The Pinnacle** (MJF, Shawn Spears, Wardlow, FTR, and Tully Blanchard).
- **The Lucha Brothers’ tag title reign** was short-lived, as they **lost the belts to Jurassic Express** in early 2022.
- **All Out 2021** is often **ranked among AEW’s best PPVs**, thanks to **Punk’s debut, Danielson’s arrival, and the Lucha Brothers’ cage match**.

---

### **Ratings & Reception**
- **Dynamite (September 8, 2021 – Post-All Out):** **1.12 million viewers** (highest since Punk’s debut).
- **Critical Reception:**
  - **Dave Meltzer (Wrestling Observer)** gave the **Lucha Brothers vs. Young Bucks match 5.25 stars** (one of the highest-rated matches in AEW history).
  - **Punk vs. Allin** was praised as a **strong return match** for Punk.
  - **Danielson vs. Omega** was called a **"dream match"** and a **technical clinic**.
- **Fan Reaction:** The event was **universally praised**, with many calling it **AEW’s best PPV at the time**.

---

### **Fun Facts & Trivia**
- This was **CM Punk’s first wrestling match in 7 years** (since his 2014 WWE departure).
- **Bryan Danielson’s debut** was kept **top secret**—even AEW wrestlers didn’t know he was signing.
- The **Steel Cage Match** was the **first in AEW history**.
- **Paul Wight (Big Show)** made his **AEW in-ring debut** at this event.
- **Miro’s TNT Title reign** (140 days) ended shortly after All Out when he **lost to Sammy Guevara**.
- **Tony Khan** called All Out 2021 **"the best PPV I’ve ever been a part of."**

---

### **Legacy of All Out 2021**
- **Marked the beginning of AEW’s "Golden Era"** (2021-2022), with **Punk, Danielson, and Cole** all debuting in a short span.
- **Proved AEW could deliver dream matches** (Danielson vs. Omega, Punk’s return).
- **Set up major storylines** for **2022**, including **Hangman Page’s rise, MJF’s heel turn, and the Elite’s dominance**.
- **Often compared to WWE’s WrestleMania** in terms of **hype and star power**.
